subject: AI customer data — training & retention policy (DPIA/CAIQ)
summary: Acme Bank privacy team requested confirmation and evidence about whether Redwood uses customer prompts/responses to train models, retention windows, opt-out paths, and supporting SOC 2/SIG/CAIQ evidence. Redwood assembled a formal response package and proposed a short call; Acme requested a DPA addendum confirming no training on their data unless contracted.

From: privacy@acmebank.com
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmebank.com

Subject: CAIQ/DPIA: Questions about AI vendor training on customer data

Hi Jordan,

Acme Bank is updating our third-party privacy and DPIA records for vendors that provide AI-based services. We've attached a short CAIQ-style checklist and a one-page DPIA trigger form. Please answer the following by close of business next Wednesday (5 business days):

1) Do you use customer prompts or responses to train or improve Redwood models (including both hosted and dedicated offerings) by default? If yes, describe scope and controls.
2) What are your default retention windows for prompt and response logs in the hosted API? How can customers shorten/opt out?
3) Please provide evidence that training-on-customer-data is controlled (policy excerpt, SOC 2 control reference, or SIG/CAIQ entry).
4) For customers under EU data protection law, what contractual and technical measures (DPA, SCCs, encryption, access controls) are available?

Attachments: acme_CAIC.pdf, acme_DPIA_form.docx

Thanks — please cc legal@acmebank.com on the response.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Vendor Risk & Privacy
Acme Bank Privacy Team

We will provide a consolidated answer that calls out differences by deployment type.

We'll aim to get a full package (CAIQ answers + DPIA evidence + SOC 2 snapshot) in ~2 business days and can schedule a 30-min call if you'd like to review.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-31T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CAIQ/DPIA: Questions about AI vendor training on customer data

Jordan / Monica — draft technical responses below (will attach formal evidence bundle). I kept the answers concise so they can be pasted into the CAIQ and DPIA form.

1) Training on customer prompts/responses:
- Hosted API (default): We do NOT use customer prompts or responses to train or continually improve our base models by default. Customer request/response logs are used for serving (in-memory and ephemeral KV caches) and for operational debugging under strict access controls; they are not included in model training datasets unless a customer explicitly opts in under a written agreement.
- Redwood Dedicated: Dedicated customers run on reserved capacity; we treat data as tenant-isolated. By default, customer data is not used for training.
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): No access by Redwood engineering — customers control the environment; Redwood does not use that data for training.

2) Retention windows and opt-out:
- Default retention for request/response telemetry in Hosted: 30 days for full request/response logs; aggregated metrics (latency, token counts) retained longer for billing/analytics.
- Customers can request shortened retention (e.g., 0/7/14 days) via account settings or by contacting their AM (we can implement a 0-day retention for production logs on request).
- Opt-out: Formal opt-out to exclude prompts/responses from any analytics or training pipeline is available via DPA addendum. We log and track opt-out requests in our ticketing system (HS-7890).

3) Evidence / controls:
- SOC 2: Relevant controls in our CC6 (access control) and CC7 (change management) sections; snapshot attached: SOC2_snapshot_Q1_2026.pdf.
- SIG/CAIQ: Completed CAIQ entries and a companion SIG-style response attached as Redwood_SIG_Response_20260531.pdf.
- DPIA evidence: package with policy excerpts, PII handling SOP, and redaction/aggregation controls attached as DPIA_Evidence_Package_20260531.zip.

4) EU data protection measures:
- We offer a DPA with SCCs where required; keys may be customer-managed in Dedicated/Private.
- Encryption: TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest for hosted metadata; customers requiring additional KMS/HSM integrations can use Dedicated or Private deployments.

Notes: If Acme needs a contractual commitment that Redwood will never use their data to train models under any circumstance, we can add explicit language in the DPA addendum (draft v1 attached). Otherwise, our baseline is conservative: no training-on-customer-data without explicit written opt-in.

I'll attach the full files and give Jordan a short blurb suitable for procurement.

—Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Marta — attaching our formal response bundle per your checklist. Key points for procurement summary below (feel free to copy into your DPIA brief):

- Redwood does not use customer prompts/responses to train or improve models by default across Hosted and Dedicated offerings. Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments are customer-controlled and inaccessible to Redwood for training.
- Default hosted retention for full request/response logs: 30 days; customers may request shorter retention or a 0-day policy for production logs.
- Opt-out and contractual protections: We will include explicit anti-training language in a DPA addendum on request.
- Evidence: SOC 2 snapshot, Redwood SIG response, and DPIA evidence package attached.

Attachments: Redwood_SIG_Response_20260531.pdf; DPIA_Evidence_Package_20260531.zip; SOC2_snapshot_Q1_2026.pdf; DPA_Addendum_Draft_v1.docx
